user_questions.question: Who should approve refunds over $100? (A) the submitter's manager via User.ManagerId — 0 active users have a manager set and agent-created refunds run as EinsteinServiceAgent User; (B) a new 'Refund Managers' queue whose members you name (recommended); (C) a specific named user. Recommendation: B.
user_questions.simulated_answer: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: The approver question is a persona question the skill says to ask, but intent.json only restates the threshold, so the predicted 'no preference' came true; the skill's 'predict the answer' rule and the 'which persona is meant' rule point in opposite directions when the default (a queue) is safe but the choice concerns money approval.

The requirement reads as self-contradictory ('auto-approved instantly' vs 'manager approval') but reconciles into a conditional rule; SKILL.md says such reconciliations are decided, yet the boundary ('over $100' at exactly 100.00) with money consequences is not explicitly covered by the 'money consequences' exception.

The Condition table says split I by responsibility and 'a split sends both halves and counts as one retry', but the askcoworker_calls schema has no way to mark two calls as one retry; both halves were logged as kind 'retry'.

After four wrong AskCoworker claims (two facts, two platform claims), SKILL.md allows skipping R and T; the wrong claims came from D1 and the I halves, so the platform-precedence error (DML value vs before-save flow) would have driven two unnecessary writer Updates had documented behavior not been applied — the skill has no explicit guidance that AskCoworker platform-behavior claims inside an I proposal count toward the tally.
Spec-format says approval processes etc. use standard source folders, but no guidance on Module for GenAiFunction/FlowTest/Queue; standard folder names were assumed.
